phase: Phase 8.3 — seek-based partial I/O: does a seeked view become a bytes-read win?

whole_file.note: Complete-cost axis is unchanged from Phase 7 and remains a loss; the seek directory is a query-capability cost, not a size win.
whole_file.non_seek_rebase_note: PDF_DEFLATE_REPLAY_RANS and BYTE_RANS are +18 B versus Phase 7 solely because the UNIVERSE string gained the +seek-directory-v1 suffix; seek_directory == false is otherwise byte-identical to the Phase-7 serialization.

strace_cross_check.relation: strace_bytes_read == instrumented bytes_read + 64 for every query
strace_cross_check.delta_explanation: The CLI reads the fixed 64-byte header to discover the seek feature before handing the handle to the seek reader; the CountingReader wraps the reader and does not count that peek. No other process read touches the descriptor.

losing_queries.reason: constant floor > gzip's read-ahead at the very start
xz's compressed prefix is small and its read-ahead minimal

notes: bytes_read is the instrumented CountingReader total (primary); strace -P attributes reads to the descriptor file only (cross-check).

The constant floor is dominated by GRAPH (265,462 B) + OBSERVATION_INDEX (146,711 B) + DIRECTORY (27,390 B); it does not shrink with output size, so it loses to a small-prefix comparator and would dominate a descriptor smaller than ~9 MB.

OS page cache changes wall time, not read() byte counts; the sequential baselines' compressed-prefix column is measured at a pipe and therefore includes a bounded read-ahead (an upper bound on the true seek cost for those decoders).

verdict: BYTES-READ WIN for mid/late queries on this large locally-generated PDF: the seeked view reads a constant 439,679-461,367 B (GRAPH+INDEX+DIRECTORY floor plus one referenced channel) regardless of offset, versus gzip's 2.7-9.8 MB compressed prefix (6-21x fewer bytes) and zstd/xz's 1.5-6.2 MB; it also drops CPU to ~0.00 s and peak RSS from ~38 MB (Phase 7) to ~3.8 MB. It LOSES on bytes at a=0 versus gzip (327,680 B) and at early queries (<= ~1.7 MB) versus xz (253,952-368,640 B) because of the constant ~0.44 MB floor. No population claim: one locally generated 33.8 MB PDF.
